archetypes.name: script-ref-tracer
archetypes.rationale: Verifies that every plan-cited line number, variable name, and function name matches actual current script content to catch stale references before implementation begins.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan cites specific line numbers (1162, 273, 1300, 1510, 339-341, 398, 408, 494-531, 533-563) and named symbols (pre_coder_path_diff_file, pre_coder_path_cached_diff_file, snapshot_pre_coder_tracked_state, round_coder_delta_paths, path_is_pre_coder_carryover, collect_round_stage_paths, round_tracked_dirty_outside_manifest, round_has_non_carryover_tracked_residue, run_implement_mav_apply) across the scope-listed scripts. Cross-check every cited line number against the actual file contents to determine whether the referenced constructs appear at or near the stated positions, and flag any symbol that is absent, renamed, or placed more than a few lines away from its cited location. Also verify the sourcing-chain claim that review-implement-step5-loop.sh sources review-and-fix.sh at line 3, confirming that pre_coder_snapshot_dir would already be in scope in that script without an additional source statement. Flag any sourcing gap that would make the helper undefined in a consuming script. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: grant-boundary
archetypes.rationale: Validates the plan's core security assumption that the proposed sibling snapshot directory is provably outside all Codex and Cursor coder write grants as expressed in the actual dispatch call sites.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan's tamper-resistance guarantee rests on the claim that a sibling directory under $IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR (parent of round_dir) is outside the Codex --add-dir grant list and outside Cursor's --workspace grant. Locate the actual coder-dispatch call sites in the scope-listed scripts and confirm exactly which --add-dir roots are passed to Codex and which --workspace root is passed to Cursor, then verify that the proposed sibling location is demonstrably unreachable given the production round_dir=$IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR/round-<N> path. Flag any dispatch path that passes $IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR itself, or any ancestor of the proposed sibling directory, as an --add-dir or --workspace root, since that would nullify the relocation guarantee. Also check whether any Cursor dispatch path in these scripts does reach round_dir or $IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR, contradicting the plan's assertion that Cursor never reached round_dir. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
